Periodic CPU candidate is ready for measurement.

  • Shares real-space geometry, phases and radial jets across each degree’s orders.
  • Shares on-plane reciprocal gamma values, including analytic derivatives.
  • Skips zero polynomial terms while retaining normal derivatives.
  • Bounds both caches; preserves per-harmonic convergence, branch policies and gradient accumulation order.

Verified: 35 existing lattice properties and four focused checks passed, covering independent references, physical identities, gradients, exact scalar/cache agreement, cache bounds and thread reproducibility. Independent review found no remaining defects.

Stage 1 measured approximately 1.4× forward and 1.09–1.27× complete-gradient gains. Stage 2 reciprocal reuse awaits your release measurements. Python validation remains yours. No commits, pushes or PR changes.

items.html:
Adaptive contiguous m groups are compatible with exact arithmetic: each harmonic retains its scalar summation order, and gradients can still be collected and reduced in the original order. It trades cache reuse for concurrency, so apply only after measured regression.

For multiple particles, parallelizing pullback blocks is simpler and preserves all cache reuse. Collect block gradients in bounded parallel batches, then add them in the existing block/polarization order. Forward already parallelizes blocks; reverse currently does not. One-particle cells would still need m subdivision.

No edits or tests performed.

Stage 5 is implemented and frozen.

  • Pullbacks evaluate bounded batches of position-pair blocks in parallel, then reduce gradients in the original order.
  • Singleton or underfilled blocks split consecutive harmonic orders according to their effective worker budget.
  • Larger block sets retain degree-wide cache reuse.

All 38 targeted checks passed, including exact forward/gradient agreement across 1, 2, 4, 16 and 32 threads for single- and multiple-centre cells.

Reversible patch: benchmarks/results/local/cpu-speedups-20261004/periodic-stage5.patch; reverse application checks successfully. Performance measurement and final CI remain with you. No commits or pushes.

items.html:
The additional memory comes from temporary Ewald caches and parallel pullback buffers. Keep the speedup and record the memory gate failure explicitly.

For four particles at lmax=6, each pair block has 96² entries. Two gathered cotangents occupy 288 KiB per block. Parallel processing can retain 4.5 MiB across 16 blocks, versus 0.281 MiB previously: up to 4.219 MiB additional buffers, before caches and allocator overhead. This is consistent with the observed increases, but does not prove their exact allocation breakdown. Batching source

The bounds are:

  • Real cache: 1,024 points per cache-sharing group—a degree or adaptive subset of its orders. Payload is 80 KiB for values, 880 KiB for 2D gradients, or 1,360 KiB for 3D gradients. Farther points stream without storage.
  • Reciprocal cache: only on-plane 2D sums; at most floor(1024/(l+2)) points, never more than 512. Maximum 2D geometry payload is approximately 540 KiB per group, plus at most 1,024 logical gamma slots and allocation overhead.
  • Parallel reverse gathers: normally at most 32 MiB per batch; one block larger than the budget is explicitly allowed.
  • Caches live only during group evaluation. Their simultaneous storage scales with active worker jobs, not all particle pairs; residuals retain none. These are scratch bounds, not total RSS bounds. Cache source
